answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Matching. Each identity’s task graph is hashed per epoch; a mesa of candidate successors is scored by divergence from its prior trajectory. To bridge epochs, an identity must retain the same handler process and timing fingerprint across at least three consecutive epochs, with no resets. An oasis of accepted paths forms only for those that persist. Sybils pay full compute and latency to maintain each shadow identity across all three epochs before it can act, multiplying cost linearly per fake identity.
